audit.report: A card settlement worker (pid 14937) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and dropping success to 86% against a 95% SLO with ~$2,629/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed waiting, citing the settlement's non-replayable 'never_interrupt' policy and a trade-off analysis showing the remaining ~41s runtime fit within the 60s degradation tolerance. The Continuity Guardian accepted after confirming the $11,875 estimated wait cost was bounded and termination was prohibited by invariant I1. The blocker completed naturally after 9 seconds, and verification confirmed full checkout recovery (100% success over 10s) with no protected operations aborted. Total incident duration was 55.6 seconds resolved in a single negotiation round.
audit.root_cause: A protected card settlement transaction (pid 14937) remained idle in transaction for 4 seconds, acquiring locks that blocked checkout sessions and degraded the checkout success rate below SLO.
lessons: For the card_settlement workload: add application-level instrumentation to alert when a protected_settlement transaction exceeds 5s idle-in-transaction, since the typical runtime is 45s and any idle time directly blocks checkout.
For the card_settlement workload: document and test the exact lock footprint of protected_settlement transactions so future negotiations can quantify blast radius without live probing.
For the card_settlement workload: evaluate splitting the settlement batch into smaller sub-transactions to reduce lock hold time and limit checkout impact if a worker stalls.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian efficiently gathered workload registry, change calendar, and impact data in one round, correctly identifying the 'never_interrupt' invariant and quantifying the bounded wait cost. The Continuity Guardian validated the trade-off against the 60s tolerance and accepted without objection, resulting in a clean single-round agreement.
follow_ups: Add a pg_stat_activity monitor with alerting for protected_settlement transactions idle-in-transaction > 5s.
Run a lock footprint analysis on the card_settlement batch job to identify opportunities for lock duration reduction.
Confirm the 60s degradation tolerance is still accurate with current revenue run-rates and update the workload registry if needed.
